transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… what finally pushed me to come in is that I just can’t seem to keep my attention where it needs to be anymore. I’m an electrician, so I’m used to juggling details, estimates, code forms, materials, measurements — all that stuff — but lately I’ll sit down to finish one estimate or fill out one form, and before I know it I’m off somewhere else mentally.

Like, a tool will make a noise in the shop, or my phone buzzes with a text, or I’ll suddenly get some idea about rearranging the workshop or fixing something that wasn’t even the job I was working on, and I’m pulled away completely. Then I come back and I’m like, “Wait, which job was this for?” or I realize I mixed up parts of one estimate with another. It’s embarrassing, honestly, because this is the kind of stuff I’m supposed to be solid at.

It’s not just being a little distracted, I guess. It’s gotten to the point where work is starting to get tangled up, and that’s what made me think, okay, I probably need to talk to someone before I mess something up worse.
When did you first start noticing these kinds of attention issues? Were you like this even as a kid, or is this something that’s developed more recently?

I’d say it’s more recent. I mean, I’ve probably always had normal moments of getting sidetracked like anybody, but this level of it — where it’s actually interfering with my work and I’m losing the thread of what I’m doing — that’s been building for about seven months now.

It kind of lines up with when we took on the mortgage for the workshop and the equipment. That’s when I first started noticing I wasn’t just “busy” or “stressed,” but actually having trouble keeping my attention pinned down long enough to finish the paperwork or stay with one task. At first I thought, okay, it’s just the adjustment, more responsibility, more moving parts. But month by month it’s felt like it’s gotten harder to ignore.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, like feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Not really “down,” no… at least that’s not how I’d describe it. It’s more like the opposite sometimes, honestly. I’ll get in this really big, charged-up mood where I’m talking fast and feeling like, okay, this is it, our little shop is about to take off — like we’re going to become the main solar outfit in town, and I can see the whole plan in my head.

And when I’m in that mood, I’m excited about everything. I’ll be laying out ideas for jobs, expansion, new equipment, all of it, like it’s obvious and everyone should be able to see it the way I do. But then if my wife pushes back, or one of the apprentices says something like, “Are you sure that’s the best way to do it?” or asks a normal question about the plan, I can just… snap. Not screaming necessarily, but I get sharp. Too sharp. Like I’ll take it as them not believing in me, or getting in the way, when later I can see they were probably just asking a reasonable question.

So it’s not that I’ve lost interest in things I like. If anything I get overly fired up about them. But the irritability part, yeah, that’s been noticeable.
Have there been times when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or so confident that you didn’t need much sleep, and this lasted for several days in a row?

Yeah… yes. That’s actually been one of the stranger parts, because normally if I only sleep three or four hours, I’d expect to feel wrecked the next day. But for months now, there’ll be stretches where I’m sleeping maybe three, maybe four hours, and then I’m just up before dawn like my body decided the night is over.

And I don’t mean I’m lying there exhausted and frustrated, staring at the ceiling. I’ll wake up and feel ready to go — like I should head straight into pricing materials, checking emails, sketching out another system layout, running numbers in my head. It feels like I got a full night’s rest even though, if you actually count the hours, I absolutely didn’t.

My wife has commented on it because I’ll be up while it’s still dark, already moving around, making coffee, grabbing a notebook, thinking I can get a jump on everything. In the moment it feels productive, like I’m ahead of the day. But yeah, it’s been going on for months, and the amount of sleep is definitely not normal for me.
Have there been times when your mood was unusually high, excited, or irritable for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a week straight?

Yes. Yeah, I’d say there have been stretches like that. It’s not just a good mood for an hour or getting excited about one job — it’ll be like I’m in this big, pumped-up state most of the day, day after day, where I’m talking like everything is finally coming together and our little shop is about to become the main solar outfit in town.

And in my head it all feels very clear, like I can see the whole thing laid out — the jobs we’re going to take, the direction we should go, how we’re going to grow. I’ll talk a lot about it, probably more than people around me want to hear, honestly. But then the flip side is, if my wife questions part of the plan, or one of the apprentices asks something pretty normal like, “Are you sure we should do it that way?” I can get sharp with them really fast.

It feels in the moment like they’re doubting me or slowing me down, even if afterward I can see they weren’t trying to do that. So, yeah, it’s this mix of excited and driven, but also really irritable if anyone pushes back even a little.

Have there been times when your mood was so high or irritable that it caused you to act differently than usual — like taking on a lot of projects at once, making big plans, or doing things more impulsively, even if they weren’t typical for you?

Yeah, definitely. That’s probably the part my wife would point to first, honestly. When I get into that mode, I’m just… going nonstop. Like I’ll go from a job site to looking at a potential bid, then come back and instead of winding down or doing normal paperwork at a normal pace, I’ll be in the workshop rewiring some test panel or messing with a setup for a home-automation idea I suddenly think we should offer.

And it’s not just one thing at a time. That’s the problem. I’ll start one idea — like, okay, we should build out a cleaner demo board for customers — and before that’s even halfway done, I’m already sketching some other smart-home control setup or pricing parts for something else. Then I’m thinking about another bid, another service we could add, another way to make the shop stand out. It feels like if I sit still, I’m wasting time, like there’s this window and I have to use every minute of it.

At the time it feels productive, like I’m finally moving fast enough. But looking at it later, yeah, I can see it’s different from how I usually am. I’m usually busy, sure, the work kind of requires that, but this is more like I can’t stop stacking things on top of each other.
Have there been times when you felt down or lost interest in things for several days in a row, or had trouble getting motivated, even when things around you were going okay?

I don’t know that I’d put it that way, honestly. I mean, I have off days like anyone — days where I’m tired or annoyed or I don’t feel like dealing with invoices or customers or crawling through another attic. But I’m not sure I’ve had, like, several days in a row where everything was fine around me and I just felt down or totally lost interest.

It’s a little hard to separate sometimes, because with work there are always stressful pieces, and motivation kind of comes and goes depending on what’s in front of me. But if you mean sitting around feeling sad for days, or not caring about things I normally care about, I can’t really say that’s been a major thing I’ve noticed. At least not in the way you’re describing.
